passage:
Monday. Bhupen stood at the foot of the slide ladder with four other children ahead of him. He hopped from foot to foot and tried to squeeze past a girl in a yellow frock. His aunt called, “Bhupen, look, everyone is waiting for a turn.” Lokesh, a boy in a red cap, stayed at the back and said nothing, hugging his knees.
Thursday. Bhupen counted the children in front out loud, “One, two, three,” and folded his arms.
Saturday. He waited through all five. His aunt clapped softly, and Bhupen whispered, “Now it’s my turn.” Lokesh, behind him, grinned.

qa.q: How many children were ahead of Bhupen in the queue on Monday?
qa.a: Four other children were ahead of him at the foot of the slide ladder.

qa.q: What was Bhupen feeling as he hopped from foot to foot on Monday?
qa.a: He felt impatient. Hopping and trying to squeeze past the girl in the yellow frock show that he wanted his turn right away.

qa.q: What small step helped Bhupen hold on while waiting on Thursday?
qa.a: Counting the children in front out loud gave him something to do with his impatience, and it made the wait feel shorter. 🙂

qa.q: What might Lokesh have been feeling, staying silent at the back on Monday?
qa.a: Lokesh may have felt uneasy watching Bhupen try to push ahead, or he may simply have been patient. His silence and hugged knees do not show for sure which.

grounding: Shows a young child slowly learning to wait for a slide turn, helped by an adult's words, counting and praise.

passage:
The bakery was hot and loud, and the line reached the door. Yusuf, five, held Papa’s hand and stared at the buns. “Why is that lady going first?” he whispered. “She came first,” said Papa. “We wait.”
Behind them a boy named Varun kept tugging his mother’s sleeve and groaning. The people in front only sighed. Yusuf’s lip wobbled. He pressed his face into Papa’s leg and counted the fan blades going round.
When the man at the counter finally nodded at them, Papa crouched down. “You waited so well.” Yusuf held out the coins.

qa.q: Who was standing behind Yusuf in the bakery line?
qa.a: A boy named Varun was behind Yusuf, tugging his mother’s sleeve and groaning.

qa.q: Why did Yusuf's lip wobble in the line?
qa.a: Yusuf was finding the wait hard. The heat, the noise and seeing the lady go first made him want to give up, so he hid his face in Papa's leg.

qa.q: How did counting the fan blades help Yusuf?
qa.a: It gave Yusuf something to do while he waited, so the impatience was easier to hold, and Papa's praise at the end told him the effort was noticed.

qa.q: How might Varun's mother feel while Varun tugs at her sleeve in the crowded line?
qa.a: She may feel tired and a little embarrassed, hoping the line moves quickly. The passage only shows the tugging and groaning, so her exact feeling is a guess.

grounding: Shows a young child waiting at a crowded counter, holding on through impatience with Papa's clear rule and praise.
